config._note: HR/labour approval record (urenstaat). A single Timesheet captures the hours an employee logged for one period plus a submit -> approve/reject -> reopen approval workflow (x-openregister-lifecycle on `status`). ADR-062 round-2 rework: (1) total-hours KPI stat top-left so the approver sees the claimed volume at a glance; (2) the data widget SPLIT into 'Time entry' (period/description/project/cost centre/billable -- what was worked) and 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason -- the workflow trail), each excluding employeeId since the Related panel already resolves and links the claiming Employee by name; (3) related alongside both, matching their combined height. Files sits full-width below for approval evidence and signed timesheets (approval documents matter, so they are on the body, not a tab). NO email/calendar/talk widgets -- the Timesheet schema declares no comms linkedTypes and a labour record does not correspond; any communication is with the person (Employee), not the record. lifecycleActions expose the schema's own submit/approve/reject/reopen transitions (guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard). Audit history is pushed to a sidebar tab as a rarely-scanned surface.

config._note: Expense-reimbursement claim (onkostendeclaratie). A single Expense holds one claim (amount / currency / category / date + attached receipt) and a submit -> approve/reject -> reimburse lifecycle (x-openregister-lifecycle on `status`). Content starts at gridY 0 with the 'Claim' data (title/description/amount/currency/category/expenseDate/receiptFile) then 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason/reimbursedAt) below it, both excluding employeeId since Related already resolves the claiming Employee by name; an amount KPI stat sits top-right so the payout figure is unmissable, with Related beneath it matching the combined left-column height. The Files widget (receipt / bon) runs full-width AFTER the domain cards, same placement convention as Timesheet's approval evidence -- the approver reads the claim record first, then opens the receipt to verify it. NO email/calendar/talk -- Expense declares no comms linkedTypes; a reimbursement claim is a financial/HR record, not a correspondence thread. lifecycleActions expose submit/approve/reject/reimburse (approve/reject guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard; reimburse is terminal). Audit history is a sidebar tab. receipt-ocr (2026-07-16): page-level action "Extract receipt data" mirrors PayslipDetail's "Genereer PDF" shape -- POST /api/expenses/extract-receipt with {expenseId: @objectId}, guarded server-side by ExpenseController::authorizeExpense() (resolve-first RBAC) then an admin-or-owner ownership check.

config._note: Hub archetype: Employee is the record every other HR/payroll schema in hrmq points AT (EmploymentContract.employeeId, Payslip.employeeId, Timesheet.employeeId, Expense.employeeId — all now canonical $ref relations, ADR-062 rule 7), so the page's job is to be the single place an HR/payroll admin lands to see one person's whole labour and pay picture. ADR-062 round-2 rework: the data widget is SPLIT into 'Person' (employeeNumber/firstName/lastName/dateOfBirth/bsn — the identity attributes) at 8-wide beside an in-grid stats-block (KPIs, top-right — replaces the deprecated summaryAggregates header chips) at 4-wide; 'Employment & compliance' (startDate/endDate/grossMonthlySalary/taxTableColor/ID-document retention/30%-ruling incl. start/end date + reduced-norm flag (30-procent-regeling)/A1 posting/jurisdiction-specific onboarding flags — 21 fields, genuinely this schema's bulk) runs full-width below since it has no natural width-4 partner. Contracts and Timesheets are paired FK-scoped lists, then Payslips (allowCreate:false — payroll-generated, not hand-created from here) and Expenses, then org-chart-basic (2026-07-13) adds an Assignments FK-scoped list (OrgAssignment.employeeId — the placements this employee holds across the org hierarchy) as a full-width row, and performance-reviews-mvp (2026-07-13) adds a Beoordelingen FK-scoped list (PerformanceReview.employeeId — the ADR-001 Rule 6 dossier anchoring: performance data lives on the personnel dossier, not a separate module) as a further full-width row, and goals-okr (2026-07-15) adds a Doelen & OKR's FK-scoped list (Objective.employeeId — the measurable, cross-review sibling of Beoordelingen; team objectives live on OrgUnit and do not appear here) as a further full-width row, and comp-cycles (2026-07-15) adds a Beloningsvoorstellen FK-scoped list (CompAdjustment.employeeId — the ADR-001 Rule 6 'Functie & comp' detail-surface anchoring: compensation-review proposals live on the personnel dossier, not a separate module) as a further full-width row, and leave-buy-sell (2026-07-15) adds a Verlof kopen/verkopen FK-scoped list (LeaveTransaction.employeeId, rowRoute LeaveTransactionDetail) as a further full-width row, before the personnel-file Files leaf, which shifts down again. Files is justified by identityDocumentVerified/identityDocumentRetainedUntil/loonheffingenVerklaringOnFile — real statutory document-retention fields on this schema, not a generic add. NO calendar/contacts/talk: Employee declares no appointment or comms linkedType — the person's own identity data lives on this record, it is not a link to a separate NC contact. No lifecycleActions — Employee carries no x-openregister-lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

config.description: Gegenereerde HR-documenten (arbeidsovereenkomst, aanbiedingsbrief, werkgeversverklaring, getuigschrift) via docudesk.

config._note: hrmq-docudesk-documents (2026-07-13): GeneratedDocument is hrmq's log of ONE docudesk render+store handoff (design.md D1), the PayrollGLPostDetail split applied to a document instead of a ledger entry -- gd-status leads with the outcome facts (status/generatedAt/errorMessage), gd-related resolves the Employee and (nullable) EmploymentContract, gd-data carries the remaining fields (documentType/templateRef/filePath) below. No lifecycleActions -- HrDocumentService drives every transition server-side, exactly the PayrollGLPostDetail precedent. Unlike every other hrmq detail page this one IS a document, so the sidebar keeps the library's default Files tab (the stored PDF -- design.md D4, 'the whole point') alongside the default Audit Trail tab, hiding only Notes/Tags/Tasks which carry no meaning here: the custom audit-only `tabs` override the rest of hrmq uses would suppress Files too (CnObjectSidebar's open-enum `tabs` widget registry has no `files` entry), so this page opts into `hiddenTabs` instead of `tabs` -- a deliberate, documented deviation from the fleet's usual sidebar convention, needed to actually show the per-object file. payslip-pdf-docudesk (2026-07-14): gd-data additionally excludes the new payslipId/jaaropgaafId $ref fields -- gd-related resolves both.

Financial-document archetype (x-schema-org: schema:Invoice), same family as Expense's amount-first design: three headline tiles (gross pay, net pay, Related-to-Employee) lead the page since that is what an employee or approver checks first, followed by the dense data widget carrying the full gross-to-net withholding breakdown (NL loonheffing/zvw/wkr, DE Lohnsteuer/Soli/Kirchensteuer, FR cotisations/PAS, US FICA/Medicare -- the schema is genuinely multi-jurisdiction: only one jurisdiction's fields populate per real record, but which one varies per payslip so a static manifest cannot cherry-pick per-instance; all fields surface via one widget, sized to its true field count and set to 4 columns full-width rather than clipped at 2). ADR-062 round-2: data widget now excludes employeeId (resolved via Related instead of raw uuid) and the height budget was corrected from the round-1 h7 (which clipped ~54 fields behind a scrollbar) to match content. Stat format uses 'number' not 'currency' because Payslip.currency varies per record (EUR/USD) and a widget's format is static. No files/calendar/comms leaves: nothing in the schema models an attachable payslip document or appointment, and Payslip carries no x-openregister-lifecycle so there are no lifecycleActions. Audit history is a sidebar tab. payslip-pdf-docudesk (2026-07-14): page-level action "Genereer PDF" mirrors EmploymentContractDetail's "Genereer arbeidsovereenkomst" shape -- POST /api/documents/generate with {payslipId: @objectId, documentType: loonstrook}, guarded server-side by DocumentController::authorizePayslip().

config.description: Wage-tax / social-security filings by period and statutory deadline.

config._note: Statutory-deadline archetype: a filing's whole purpose is 'was it filed on time and is proof retained'. loonaangifte-filing-lifecycle (2026-07-12) gave NL filings a real create->review->confirm->send workflow, so the page now leads with a compact status/tijdvakcode/deadline/response widget (fi-status) before the full filing data widget, and exposes the klaarzetten/bevestigen/verzenden/heropenen/corrigeren transitions via lifecycleActions (Timesheet pattern). No stats-block KPI tile is used for Status/Deadline: the vendored app-manifest-v2 schema's stat/stats-block `metric` only supports count/sum aggregation, which cannot echo a non-numeric field (enum/date) of the current object, so fi-status is a `data` widget instead -- schema-valid and functionally equivalent (prominent, top-of-page). No related panel (the schema carries no employeeId/administrationId or any other object-FK -- a filing is an organisation-level record, not scoped to a person). Files is included full-width for the filed submission/deposit proof, justified by the schema's own retainedUntil/furnishedToRecipientDate/filedWithAuthorityDate retention-evidence fields (NL 7yr / DE 6yr / US 4yr retention obligations). No calendar/comms leaves -- deadline is a plain date field, not an appointment/event linkedType. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: UPA (Uniforme Pensioenaangifte) deliveries by period and sector fund, gated on the referenced payroll run's approval.

config._note: pension-filing-upa-mvp (2026-07-12): same statutory-filing shape as LoonaangifteFilingDetail (create->review->confirm->send, gated on an external precondition), but this schema ALSO carries a real FK (payrollRunId -> PayrollRun, the run the delivery reports on), so the layout follows the TimesheetDetail split instead: pf-status leads top-left with the prominent status/deadline/response facts, pf-related sits top-right at matching height to resolve and link the referenced PayrollRun, then pf-data runs below with the remaining record fields (period/fund/aanleverkenmerk/verzondenDoor), excluding payrollRunId since Related already resolves it. Same reasoning as loonaangifte for NOT using a stats-block: the vendored app-manifest-v2 schema's stat/stats-block `metric` only supports count/sum aggregation over a collection, which cannot echo a non-numeric field (enum/date) of the current object, so pf-status is a `data` widget instead -- schema-valid and functionally equivalent (prominent, top-of-page). No Files leaf: unlike LoonaangifteFiling, PensionFiling carries no retention/proof-of-filing fields (no retainedUntil/furnishedToRecipientDate equivalent) -- the response is captured in-record (responseStatus/responseMessage), not as an attached document. No calendar/comms leaves -- deadline is a plain date field, not an appointment/event linkedType. lifecycleActions expose controleren/bevestigen/verzenden/heropenen/corrigeren, controleren guarded server-side by PayrollRunApprovedGuard. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Jaarlijkse WNT-verantwoording per topfunctionaris: de bezoldiging per jaar en de publicatiestatus. De verzameling regels van een jaar IS de WNT-verantwoording van dat jaar (wnt-disclosure).

config._note: wnt-disclosure: the annual WNT-verantwoording record for one topfunctionaris (PensionFilingDetail shape -- a per-period disclosure carrying a real FK, employeeId -> Employee). wd-status leads top-left with the year/totalCompensation/status facts; wd-related sits top-right at matching height to resolve and link the referenced topfunctionaris Employee (whose wntTopfunctionaris/wntUitzonderingReden drive the nl-wnt-norm-overschrijding audit); wd-data runs below with the remaining fields excluding employeeId since Related already resolves it. No stats-block (the vendored schema's metric only aggregates over a collection, cannot echo a scalar field of the current object -- PensionFilingDetail reasoning). No Files/comms/calendar leaves -- the disclosure carries no attached-document/appointment fields. lifecycleActions expose the single publiceren transition (concept -> gepubliceerd, no guard). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Run-to-run loonmutatie-rapporten: per periode wie is ingestroomd/uitgestroomd en de totale loonkostenverandering (payroll-mutation-reports). Admin/HR only -- gegenereerd via de "Mutatieoverzicht"-actie op een loonrun of via occ hrmq:payroll:mutations --persist.

config._note: payroll-mutation-reports (2026-07-14): a PayrollMutationReport is a PURE, read-only diff snapshot -- never recomputed, never written outside PayrollMutationService (design.md D3) -- so the page leads with the accountant's headline (totalWageCostDelta) plus the entered/left/changed counts as stat KPIs (the PayrollRunDetail stat-tile precedent), then the full record (header fromRunId/toRunId/fromPeriod/toPeriod/administrationId/generatedAt, the four component deltas, the four counts, and the embedded per-employee `lines` array) in the pmr-data widget below -- the PayrollGLPostDetail precedent for an embedded array snapshot rendered inside a plain data widget (its own `lines` field, same shape: a system-generated audit-style record, not user-editable). No lifecycleActions: the schema carries no x-openregister-lifecycle -- a report is either regenerated (superseding this one in place, design.md D7) or not; there is no user-facing status transition to guard. No Files/calendar/comms leaves -- not a document or event. Admin/HR only, mirroring the Payroll nav group.

config.description: Payroll-to-GL posting attempts: one balanced loonjournaalpost handed off to shillinq per approved loonrun.

config._note: payroll-glpost-shillinq (2026-07-12): a PayrollGLPost is hrmq's log of ONE handoff attempt into shillinq's JournalEntry register -- never the journal itself (design.md D1). TimesheetDetail/PensionFilingDetail split: pg-status leads top-left with the prominent outcome facts (status/postedAt/errorMessage), pg-related sits top-right to resolve and link the referenced PayrollRun (a real $ref, unlike journalEntryId), then pg-data runs below with the remaining record fields including the journalNumber/journalEntryId pointer into shillinq (plain display only -- no cross-app deep link in MVP, per design.md's 'posted != materialised' risk note) and the lines snapshot. NO lifecycleActions: status has no x-openregister-lifecycle transition map -- PayrollGLPostService drives every transition server-side from `occ hrmq:glpost:run`, exactly the PayrollRunDetail precedent (never invent a user-facing transition the backend does not guard). pages.title: Simuleer loonstrook
pages._note: proforma-payslip design.md D6: manifest v2 has no declarative primitive for a persist-nothing interactive compute-form. open-form is bound to a register/schema and PERSISTS the created object -- exactly what a pro-forma simulation must not do. api-call only interpolates fixed/@token params against a form-less trigger and surfaces a toast + page refresh -- it cannot gather a bespoke set of hypothetical inputs (bruto, tabel, geboortedatum, deeltijdfactor, bijzondere beloning, periode) nor render the returned JSON breakdown. So this page is a host-app SFC (ProformaPayslip.vue, registered in src/registry.js) that renders the input form and calls POST /api/payroll/proforma directly, showing the full gross-to-net breakdown. No register/schema is referenced and no object is ever created -- the stable, test-covered contract is the endpoint (PayrollController::proforma) + the hrmq:payroll:proforma occ command.

config.description: Zie of je loon als DGA voldoet aan de gebruikelijkloonnorm -- zonder accountant of occ-tool.
config._note: single-person-modes (REQ-SPM-006/D5): a self-service surface for the EXISTING nl-gebruikelijkloon-norm verdict for the caller's own DGA Employee. The whole menu entry is visibleIf-gated on administrationMode: dga_single_person (D2/D3). The warning banner is bound to the read-only, stateless GET /apps/hrmq/api/payroll/dga-status endpoint (PayrollController::dgaStatus, which REUSES NlDgaChecks' predicate -- zero new tax logic, zero new persistence): visibleWhen {endpoint, field: met, op: eq, value: false} renders it only when the caller's own annualised loon is below norm AND unjustified. The endpoint takes no per-object parameter (it always means 'my own record', D5.1), so the visibleWhen.endpoint non-templated same-origin path applies cleanly -- no object id to interpolate, the documented fallback (a custom widget) is not needed. Fail-safe: the banner stays hidden on a 404 (no Employee, or Employee not a DGA -- both collapse to the same status, D5.1) or any fetch failure, so a non-DGA caller who somehow reaches this route sees no alert. The info banner is always visible and explains the page. Both widgets are built-in `banner` (CnBannerWidget) -- no custom component, no single-widget-dashboard anti-pattern.

props.text: Als directeur-grootaandeelhouder (DGA) moet je jezelf minimaal het gebruikelijk loon uitbetalen. Ligt je loon eronder zonder vastgelegde onderbouwing, dan zie je hieronder een waarschuwing.
Je loon ligt onder de gebruikelijkloonnorm en er is geen onderbouwing vastgelegd. Verhoog je maandloon of leg een onderbouwing vast op je werknemersrecord.

pages.title: Administraties
pages._note: multi-administratie design.md D4/D5 (REQ-MULTI-006): the ADR-001 Rule 3 active-administratie indicator + switch, homed under Configuratie as a SETTING surface (never a per-tenant menu duplication). The manifest v2 renderer chrome exposes no topbar-switcher slot (the known v2 renderer chrome gap), and no declarative primitive can gather the caller's accessible administraties, POST a guarded switch, and re-scope sibling pages -- open-form persists a register object (wrong: the active pointer is a per-user IConfig value, not domain data) and api-call cannot render the returned accessible-administration list. So this page is a host-app SFC (AdministrationSwitcher.vue, registered in src/registry.js) calling GET/POST /api/administration/* (AdministrationController, no-admin-idor guarded server-side). The true topbar chrome slot is a named upstream nc-vue fast-follow; the sibling hrmq-ia-navigation-alignment change owns the Configuratie menu-9 drawer -- this page lands under it as a clean union (neither re-declares the group).

config._note: hris-api-public (2026-07-18): a governance/audit record of one external system granted access to hrmq via OpenRegister's public REST surface. The 'Integratie' data widget carries the whole record (name/purpose/nextcloudUserId/grantedSchemas/status/reviewedBy/reviewedAt/createdAt); no exclude, because IntegrationAccount carries NO $ref field (nextcloudUserId is a plain string per ADR-062 rule 7, never a $ref to an Employee), so there is no Related panel to resolve. NO lifecycleActions: status is a plain actief/ingetrokken enum with no x-openregister-lifecycle transition map (the OrgUnitDetail/ShiftDetail precedent) -- toggling it records a governance state, it does not run a guarded workflow, and it changes NOTHING about actual access (design.md D2). No stat/files/calendar/comms leaves -- a catalog record has no numeric headline aggregate, document, appointment, or correspondence thread. Audit history stays a sidebar tab so a reviewer can see who changed the catalog record and when. Alleen-beheerder surface (like DsrRequestDetail); enforcement is server-side OpenRegister RBAC, not a manifest flag.

config._note: rostering (2026-07-14): the publishable roster header. Unlike PayrollRun, Roster carries a REAL x-openregister-lifecycle (concept <-> gepubliceerd via publiceren/intrekken), so RosterDetail legitimately renders a lifecycleActions widget for exactly those two transitions -- no invented edge (the AttendanceRecordDetail sluiten/heropenen precedent). The 'Rooster' data widget carries period/administrationId/status; Related resolves and links the optional orgUnitId scope (excluded from data). The page-level 'ATW-controle' api-call action posts {rosterId: @objectId} to POST /api/roster/check (guarded server-side by RosterController::authorizeRoster()) and surfaces the Arbeidstijdenwet verdict over the roster's assignments regardless of publish status -- publishing itself is NOT hard-blocked on a violation (guard wiring is hrmq-rule-compliance-enforcement's scope, design.md Non-Goal). The FK-scoped 'Roosterindelingen' child object-list (RosterAssignment.rosterId = @objectId) is the plan itself. No stat KPI -- a header has no numeric headline. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: AVG (GDPR) data-subject-rights verzoeken: inzage/portabiliteit, verwijdering (retention-guarded via de statutaire bewaarplicht) en rectificatie, uitgevoerd via OpenRegister's DsarService onder een expliciet vastgestelde beheerderssessie (avg-dsr). Alleen-beheerder surface.

config._note: avg-dsr (2026-07-16): guarded api-call actions, NOT lifecycleActions -- DsrRequest.status carries no x-openregister-lifecycle map (design.md D3/D5): every transition requires a caller-role check (admin-ONLY, deliberately never widened to isAdminOrHr -- DsarService::assertPrivileged() hard-requires actual IGroupManager::isAdmin()) plus an explicitly-established DsarService-privileged session plus, for verwijdering, the statutory-retention guard (REQ-DSR-005) -- a retention-locked object (e.g. a Payslip inside its AWR 7-year window) is NEVER erased, always reported labelled 'retained (wettelijke bewaarplicht)'. Bevestig verwijdering REQUIRES a prior Voorbeeld verwijdering recorded on the SAME request (REQ-DSR-006). The Rectificeer action's `changes` payload is not yet collected via a prompt (the manifest v2 api-call action type has no free-text field-map prompt) -- the LoonbeslagDetail withdraw `reason` precedent; a prompt-collecting modal is a named fast-follow (README). Admin-only surface -- one notch stricter than the Payroll group's admin/HR posture. Audit history is a sidebar tab.
